---
title: "Connect your backend"
description: "Create a scan and authorize your customer to capture a document."
---

Add an authenticated endpoint that the Web SDK can call when a customer starts or resumes capture. Your endpoint creates a scan, requests a capture token, and returns the SDK initialization data.

## Configure your credentials

<Note>
  Keep API credentials on your backend. The React app receives only the authorization needed for its capture.
</Note>

Keep these values in your backend environment:

```bash
BOUNCR_API_URL=https://api.bouncr.io
BOUNCR_API_TOKEN=your_api_access_token
BOUNCR_VENUE_ID=your_venue_id
BOUNCR_CAPTURE_ORIGIN=https://app.example.com
```

Use the API environment supplied for your integration. Register the exact origin that serves your capture page, including the port for local development.

Your API credential needs `scans:create` and `scans:capture`. Add `scans:results:read` when this backend also retrieves results.

## Create a scan

Send the venue ID to Bouncr:

```bash
curl "$BOUNCR_API_URL/v1/scans" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOUNCR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"venue_id\":\"$BOUNCR_VENUE_ID\"}"
```

The API returns `201 Created` with the scan ID:

```json
{ "id": "128000000000000001" }
```

Store this ID on the customer’s application or onboarding record. Reuse it as the customer selects a document and completes capture.

## Add the authorization endpoint

The SDK calls your endpoint with its capture key and the customer’s document selection. Forward those values to Bouncr for the scan associated with the signed-in customer.

This Express example belongs after your application’s authentication and session middleware. `req.user` identifies the signed-in customer; `req.session` is their server-side session. It uses one scan per onboarding session. For multiple applications per customer, store the scan ID on the corresponding application record instead.

Install the supplied SDK package on the backend to use `@bouncr/capture/server`. Enable JSON request parsing before the route.

```javascript
import express from 'express';
import { encodeConfiguration } from '@bouncr/capture/server';

app.use(express.json());

const apiUrl = process.env.BOUNCR_API_URL;
const apiToken = process.env.BOUNCR_API_TOKEN;
const venueId = process.env.BOUNCR_VENUE_ID;
const captureOrigin = process.env.BOUNCR_CAPTURE_ORIGIN;

app.post('/capture/authorize', async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    if (!req.user || !req.session) return res.sendStatus(401);
    if (req.get('origin') !== captureOrigin) return res.sendStatus(403);

    const headers = {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    };
    let scanId = req.session.bouncrScanId;
    if (!scanId) {
      const created = await fetch(`${apiUrl}/v1/scans`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify({ venue_id: venueId }),
      });
      if (!created.ok) return res.sendStatus(created.status);
      scanId = (await created.json()).id;
      req.session.bouncrScanId = scanId;
    }

    const { thumbprint, country, documentType } = req.body;
    const response = await fetch(`${apiUrl}/v1/scans/${scanId}/capture-authorizations`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers,
      body: JSON.stringify({
        origin: captureOrigin,
        capture_key_thumbprint: thumbprint,
        country,
        document_type: documentType,
      }),
    });
    if (!response.ok) return res.sendStatus(response.status);

    res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-store').json({
      authorization: await response.text(),
      configuration: encodeConfiguration(apiUrl, scanId),
    });
  } catch (error) {
    next(error);
  }
});
```

The SDK forwards `authorization` and `configuration` internally. Return these values unchanged from the browser’s `authorize` callback, as shown in the [React quickstart](/external/web).

For a fresh application, create a fresh scan. For a refresh or interrupted capture, recover the existing ID from your application/session record.
